newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, seen stable after rating.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, seen stable after rating.

text.p: Croatian stocks closed mixed on Friday in brisk trade due to stronger buying, and the market was seen as consolidating fully after the country was awarded its first rating of BBB-.
Traders predicted solid gains in most liquid stocks which are still trading below the book value.
"It is nice to see the market awakening," said Dubravko Zganec, head of trading at Fima, one of the most active brokerages in 1996.

He added that some issues were emerging as definite candidates for official bourse listing and cited as most serious candidates food processor Podravka, seaside hoteliers Plava Laguna, Jadranturist and Istraturist.
Some of Croatia's leading bank stocks that are not currently traded could also squeeze their way in, Zganec said.
Five of 11 active issues rose on Friday, two dipped and four remained flat. Volume tripled to 15,865 shares, pushing turnover up to 10.6 million kuna from 2.9 million on Thursday.
Zagrebacka Banka's C-series bearer shares, rising 120 kuna from Wednesday's 480, led gainers with only 10 units sold.
But Podravka stole the show for the second time this week, selling a total of 6,405 shares at 265-275 kuna to close 10 kuna higher at 264. Its issued value is 300 kuna.

As investors skimmed recent profits, Zagrebacka's ordinary stock shed 99 kuna, to end at 1,601 on volume of 3,149. They peaked at 1,800 kuna during the session, but some of the market participants described the price as "blown up".
Zagrebacka GDRs, issued at 10 to each share, also fell from this week's peak to $29.375 from $29.75 on Seaq.
Another blue chip Pliva pharmaceuticals whose rise has been more subdued recently, added seven kuna to 547 with 3,352 units changing hands. Its 1/5 GDRs moved down to $17.06/12 from $18.40.
Laguna stocks gained 50 kuna to end the week at 1,250. Istraturist and Jadranturist were flat at 200 and 290 kuna, respectively -- each selling a few hundred shares.
Chocolate maker Kras, rumoured to have put off a deal on investment with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), dipped 10 kuna to 480 on volume of 350.
